phase: Phase 5 — height attribution of the low-gamma rigidity excess, and re-derivation of P1's corroboration line
anti_claim_s0: Nothing here estimates Lambda; nothing bears on RH. zeta is a calibrator substrate.
WHY_THIS_PHASE_AND_NOT_A_SEPARATE_RE_DER: P1's arc-summary line -- 'corroborated at the short scale by an orthogonal statistic' -- currently rests on nothing verified: its short-L figures were re-slotted (both poly9, sign inverted), its long-L companion is shown to be a fitted-unfold artifact, and the replacement bracket is R-010, which was held. There is exactly one bracketed short-L Sigma^2 number in existence and this phase produces it. Re-deriving the corroboration is therefore not an alternative to running R-010; it is downstream of it. Until this phase returns, P1 is ONE WITNESS, UNCORROBORATED, and the arc summary overclaims.

PRE_RUN_REFRAME_OF_R-010.as_registered: 'more rigid than homogeneous GUE' is degenerate with height-mixing -- is the excess real or an artifact?
PRE_RUN_REFRAME_OF_R-010.corrected_before_running: That framing is wrong, and the correction sharpens the question. With an EXACT unfold the smooth density is removed exactly, so heterogeneity of the FLUCTUATIONS cannot manufacture rigidity: Sigma^2 averages over window positions, so the block's Sigma^2 is the MEAN LOCAL rigidity over gamma in [14, 2515]. The excess is therefore real. What is in doubt is not its existence but its ADDRESS.
PRE_RUN_REFRAME_OF_R-010.the_actual_question: WHICH HEIGHT OWNS IT. 'gamma_mid = 1420' labels an average over a range whose bottom is gamma = 14.1. If, as P1 asserts, the rigidity excess grows as gamma falls, that average is dominated by the bottom of the block and the label is off by an order of magnitude in gamma. This is an attribution/slot question, which is this program's dominant error mode.
PRE_RUN_REFRAME_OF_R-010.and_it_applies_to_P1_ITSELF: P1's 2.4-sigma <r~> excess was measured on the SAME block (gamma 14.1 -> 2515.3, W=2000). So P1 carries the identical attribution exposure. Both statistics get the same decomposition in this phase.

DESIGN.primary: Sub-block decomposition of zeros6[:2000] into 4 x 500 consecutive levels. Per sub-block, on its OWN exact-theta density backbone: (a) Sigma^2 via the theta path at L in {1,2,4,8} against a curvature-matched GUE band (B=20) built at that sub-block's backbone; (b) <r~> against a matched-density GUE null (B=20) built the same way. Report excess per sub-block against that sub-block's gamma_mid.
DESIGN.resolution_check: repeat at 8 x 250 to confirm the trend is not an artifact of the split.
DESIGN.two_families_one_dataset: Sigma^2 and <r~> are different statistic families (§0d: <r~> reaches higher-order correlations), so they are two witnesses ON THE ATTRIBUTION QUESTION. They are NOT two independent witnesses in the data sense -- it is one block read twice. Stated here so it cannot be upgraded later.
DESIGN.known_residual_confound_DECLARED: sub-block 1 spans gamma 14.1 -> ~430, which is itself ~5x in density. Sub-blocking narrows the averaging range; it does not eliminate it. The claim available from this design is a TREND across sub-blocks, not a point measurement at any one height.

GATES_THAT_RUN_BEFORE_ANY_ZETA_READING.G1_separation: the curvature-matched GUE band at N=500 must have sd(L=1) < 0.016, so that the full-block gap (zeta 0.3112 vs GUE 0.3433, i.e. 0.032) is at least 2 sigma per sub-block. If not, the decomposition cannot resolve the trend at this N -- report compute-blocked and stop.

G2_powered_falsifier.construction: build a DESIGNED heterogeneous synthetic on zeta's exact-theta backbone: sub-block 1 super-rigid, sub-blocks 2-4 GUE. Push it through the identical pipeline.
G2_powered_falsifier.must_show: the decomposition LOCALIZES the rigidity to sub-block 1 (>3 sigma below its own band) while sub-blocks 2-4 sit within +/-2 sigma, AND the full-block read shows a diluted intermediate excess.
G2_powered_falsifier.argument_it_could_fire: at N=500 the per-sub-block band is ~2x wider than at N=2000. If that width swamps the contrast, every sub-block reads flat and the method returns H_flat REGARDLESS of the truth -- i.e. the instrument would answer the question by construction. This gate constructs the very answer it must detect, so a failure is a live outcome and not a formality. If it fails, H_flat becomes uninterpretable and the phase halts.

H_bottom.statement: the excess is concentrated at the bottom of the block and decays with gamma_mid
H_bottom.numeric_sigma2: sub-block 1 (gamma_mid ~ 150) Sigma^2 excess at L=1 >= 4 sigma below its band; sub-block 4 (gamma_mid ~ 2300) within 2 sigma; |excess| monotone decreasing across the four
H_bottom.numeric_rtilde: sub-block 1 <r~> excess >= 2 sigma above its matched null; sub-block 4 < 1 sigma; monotone
H_bottom.if_true_means: the excess is real but MIS-ADDRESSED. 'low gamma' in P1/P3 means gamma <~ 500, not gamma ~ 1420. P1's corroboration is RE-DERIVED and simultaneously RE-SLOTTED, and every downstream height-attribution in the arc inherits the correction.

H_flat.statement: all four sub-blocks show comparable excess
H_flat.if_true_means: 'gamma_mid = 1420' is a fair label and P1's corroboration stands as filed at the block level. NOTE: only interpretable if G2 passed.

H_null.statement: no sub-block shows excess although the full block does
H_null.if_true_means: the full-block excess is a pooling/mixing artifact after all, contradicting the reframe above. Phase 3's short-L reading AND P1's corroboration both FALL and must be refiled. This would also falsify my pre-run reframe, which is the outcome most in my own disfavour and is therefore stated first in the report if it occurs.

H_split.statement: Sigma^2 localizes to the bottom but <r~> does not, or vice versa
H_split.if_true_means: the two families DISAGREE on attribution. Corroboration is NOT re-derived and the arc-summary line must be WITHDRAWN, not weakened.

SENSITIVITY_PRIOR.rule_applied: program-measured 4-for-4 conservative; shift up one notch from instinct. Point-estimate lean is separately 5-for-5 conservative, so numeric point predictions above are stated at the optimistic edge of instinct.
SENSITIVITY_PRIOR.instinct: MEDIUM -- can 500-level sub-blocks resolve a 0.032 gap?

SPECIFICITY_PRIOR.rule_applied: HOLD FIXED. No leak from the sensitivity correction.
SPECIFICITY_PRIOR.reason: each sub-block's bracket is built on that sub-block's OWN exact-theta backbone, so the density confound is closed exactly and per-cell rather than pooled. The residual, declared above, is that a sub-block is still an average over its own ~5x density range at the bottom. The G2 falsifier constructs the confound it must detect, which is the strongest specificity evidence this program has found available.

FAILURE_CONDITIONS_WRITTEN_BEFORE_THE_RU: G1 fails -> compute-blocked, stop, do not read zeta.
G2 fails -> the decomposition cannot localize a KNOWN localized signal; H_flat is uninterpretable; halt and report the instrument limit rather than a zeta result.
H_null -> my pre-run reframe is falsified; report that FIRST, before any other result.
H_split -> withdraw the corroboration line outright; do not weaken it and do not average the two families.
Any outcome -> P1's corroboration line is rewritten from THESE numbers or deleted. It is not left standing on the superseded ones.
